relevance_note: Whole-genome sequencing of JIA multiplex pedigrees found NOD2 variants in four families described individually by pedigree and relation, and the authors state: "Our study reports an additional four families with Blau syndrome, previously ascertained as JIA."
method_note: Table 2 (families with concordant GEM results) gives one NOD2 variant per pedigree (1,017, 1,130, 207, 1,022) as GRCh37 coordinates; no cDNA, protein or transcript is tied to a specific pedigree. The Discussion names R334W (two families), R334Q (one family) and R587C (one family) but never says which pedigree carries which, so protein fields for the pedigree carriers are left null rather than matched by coordinate. The paper gives no individual labels, so carriers are 'unnamed person k' in order of first mention and untyped relatives use rule 2. The eight heterozygous siblings ('Eight siblings across four families were heterozygous') were allocated two per family: pedigrees 1,022, 1,017 and 207 each have 'two affected siblings', which leaves the sequenced twin sister and the son in pedigree 1,130 (only one twin was sequenced); that allocation is arithmetic, not stated per person. Affected parents (mothers in 1,130, 1,022, 1,017; father in 207) get individual rows but no variant rows: Table 2 says parents were genotyped and the text says the families appear to show autosomal dominant transmission, but the paper never states that a named parent carries the variant, so inheritance is 'not reported'. The unsequenced twin sister has no variant row. The 'three additional extended maternal relatives' of pedigree 1,130 are mentioned only as a count without any individual detail and get no rows. JIA for the 1,130 members is stated in the family-history sentence; for siblings in 1,022, 1,017 and 207 it is inferred from 'affected siblings' in a JIA cohort (group statement). The affected parents in 1,022, 1,017 and 207 have no feature rows because affected parent phenotypes in the cohort were JIA, RA or general autoimmunity and the paper does not say which. The singleton (unnamed person 9) is the one NOD2 indel found in the external singleton/trio cohort; the Results genomic indel and the Discussion frameshift N637Sfs*120 (19-bp deletion, replication cohort) are linked because the paper says only one NOD2 variant was found in that cohort. ClinVar status mentioned by the authors (pedigree 1,022 variant reported as VUS in ClinVar) is the paper's text, recorded only in this note; the authors themselves call it likely pathogenic. cohort_size_as_stated uses the 59 JIA cases of the multiplex cohort (99 sequenced individuals including parents; 115 external singletons). Built with a short Python script; spans checked verbatim by script. No contradictions found.
